focuses.title: The Republic at Ten
focuses.description: The republic has survived its first decade, but its common institutions no longer command the confidence of both communities. Independence needs a functioning political settlement as well as international recognition.

focuses.title: Cabinet Government
focuses.description: A cabinet answerable for security, expenditure and negotiations can reduce the personal burden on the presidency. A stronger centre also needs a larger permanent secretariat.

focuses.title: Presidential Mediation
focuses.description: Makarios can arbitrate between parliamentary allies, the Church and the security services. Personal authority accelerates decisions but leaves oversight dependent on the presidency.

focuses.title: Parliamentary Scrutiny
focuses.description: Stronger parliamentary scrutiny can build confidence in public decisions. Ministers must accept slower negotiations and less freedom to govern through presidential understandings.

focuses.title: Church Mediation
focuses.description: The Orthodox Church has land, schools and an authority that reaches beyond party organizations. Its mediation can protect independence while reinforcing expectations of public support for religious institutions.

focuses.title: Audit Office
focuses.description: An independent audit office will examine procurement and public contracts. The initial expense buys administrative savings while the parliamentary route retains its slower political bargaining.

focuses.title: Protect the Ballot
focuses.description: Electoral competition must not become a contest over who controls the police or the polling station. Protected campaigning and impartial administration can make lawful opposition credible.

focuses.title: Constitutional Talks
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 40.
focuses.description: Representatives of both communities must debate executive powers, representation and security. Opening a conference commits the government to negotiations without deciding their result.

focuses.title: The 1960 Balance
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 65. Proposed safeguards receive a communal response event.
focuses.description: A repaired partnership can retain the constitutional framework of independence. Restored vetoes and communal protections constrain executive action in exchange for stronger guarantees.
preview_effects: If the constitutional terms are accepted:

focuses.title: A Federal Compact
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 65. Both delegations and all treaty parties receive response events.
focuses.description: A negotiated federal settlement can distribute powers more explicitly between a common government and communal authorities. The additional institutions impose a lasting administrative cost.
preview_effects: If the constitutional terms are accepted:

focuses.title: Communal Rights
focuses.requirements: The selected constitutional agreement is ratified by both communal delegations.
focuses.description: Rights to representation, worship, education and legal protection must survive changes of government. Their enforcement will be entrusted to institutions accepted by both communities.

focuses.title: A Durable Republic
focuses.requirements: The agreed institutions operate and the country is at peace.
focuses.description: The republic can replace emergency improvisation with an accepted constitutional order. The settlement does not erase political disagreement or transfer territory by decree.

focuses.title: Resume the Talks
focuses.description: Clerides and Denktash have been conducting intercommunal talks since 1968. A permanent liaison channel can keep local disputes from becoming another general confrontation.

focuses.title: Safe Civilian Passage
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 40.
focuses.description: Agreed routes for workers, patients and goods can reconnect communities. Liaison staff and supervised crossings cost money and require security services to relinquish some discretion.

focuses.title: Retain Security Checks
focuses.description: Security checkpoints can reassure exposed villages and preserve inspection powers. They also obstruct ordinary commerce and deepen suspicion of the central government.

focuses.title: Joint Medical Access
focuses.description: Access to hospitals and emergency treatment can become a practical common interest. The state must fund transport, interpreters and care without discriminatory restrictions.

focuses.title: Local Security Liaison
focuses.description: Joint incident reporting can improve security without pretending that the communities already share a trusted command structure. Separate liaison offices will remain an administrative burden.

focuses.title: Reconnect Utilities
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 40. The state is owned and controlled. Both communal delegations accept the works. State146 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native infrastructure capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Electricity, water and road access should not depend on bargaining at every local checkpoint. A supervised infrastructure programme can improve services while leaving constitutional claims for negotiation.

focuses.title: Shared Municipal Funds
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 50. Both communal delegations accept the municipal funding terms.
focuses.description: A common fund can direct investment to neglected districts under joint supervision. Reliable funding reduces local uncertainty but creates an enduring budget commitment.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Communal Autonomy
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 50. Both communal delegations accept the division of local powers.
focuses.description: Recognized communal administrative powers may provide security without demanding immediate institutional integration. The common government must accept a narrower field of direct authority.

focuses.title: Joint Accounts
focuses.description: Published accounts can show how communal funds are divided and used. Common supervision makes future investment easier to defend to taxpayers in both communities.

focuses.title: Shared Representation
focuses.requirements: Both communal delegations accept their representation arrangements.
focuses.description: Reserved representation cannot become effective through a unilateral appointment. Negotiated participation must give the Turkish Cypriot community a credible voice in shared decisions.

focuses.title: Open Island Routes
focuses.requirements: Communal confidence at least 65. Communal confidence at least 65. Both delegations accept the mobility and administrative settlement.
focuses.description: A durable mobility agreement can remove the economic penalties of fragmentation. It requires functioning local guarantees rather than an assertion that the communal dispute has disappeared.

focuses.title: Enforce the Safeguards
focuses.description: A standing review commission can investigate violations and preserve confidence when a government changes. The commission adds expense but gives ordinary grievances a lawful remedy.

focuses.title: The Officer Question
focuses.description: Greek officers provide military expertise while Athens is ruled by a junta. The presidency must decide how much of the National Guard command it can safely leave dependent on an external government.

focuses.title: Cypriot Command
focuses.description: Replacing exposed commanders can strengthen loyalty to the republic. The change disrupts existing chains of command and slows training while Cypriot officers gain experience.

focuses.title: Retain Greek Missions
focuses.description: A renewed Greek training mission can improve the Guard quickly. Acceptance leaves Cyprus dependent on officers whose government may pursue a different political objective.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Police Counterweights
focuses.description: A lawful police reserve can prevent the Guard from monopolizing armed power. Rival chains of command must be coordinated and supported from the public budget.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Written Mission Terms
focuses.requirements: The Greek Training Mission agreement is active.
focuses.description: Written terms for postings, training and withdrawal can moderate dependence on Greek officers. The agreement improves accountability while retaining the mission and its political risks.

focuses.title: Expose Armed Networks
focuses.description: Investigations can disrupt clandestine violence, including the National Front and later EOKA B. Arrests and searches also risk polarizing Greek Cypriot politics.

focuses.title: Consult the Guarantors
focuses.description: The Treaty of Guarantee calls for consultation when its obligations are threatened. Greece, Turkey and Britain must each choose whether to cooperate in restoring constitutional government.
preview_effects: Greece, Turkey, United Kingdom: Guarantor Consultations

focuses.title: Presidential Safeguards
focuses.description: A protected communications network and clear succession orders can help the legal government survive a sudden attack. Preparedness is useful only if loyal institutions act when the crisis comes.

focuses.title: Restore Civilian Rule
focuses.requirements: The coup threat is resolved. Cyprus has a civilian government and is at peace.
focuses.description: A failed coup or a negotiated restoration must be followed by a command settlement and the dismantling of armed political networks. Neither a calendar date nor a foreign promise is enough.

focuses.title: The Geneva Conference
focuses.requirements: A guarantor crisis, coup or armed conflict has actually occurred.
focuses.description: A crisis conference can seek a ceasefire, constitutional restoration and practical guarantees. If negotiations fail, the involved states retain control over their next military and diplomatic choices.
preview_effects: Greece, Turkey, United Kingdom: Ceasefire and Constitutional Restoration

focuses.title: The Second Plan
focuses.description: The Second Five-Year Plan has supported roads, utilities and productive investment. Completing its priorities can sustain the growth already achieved during the 1960s.

focuses.title: Technical Institutes
focuses.description: A small island needs engineers, technicians and administrators as well as labour. Technical institutes address specialist shortages through education rather than restricting the national workforce.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: A Visitor Economy
focuses.requirements: Cyprus is at peace.
focuses.description: Hotels and visitor services can earn foreign exchange and employ a growing urban population. Concentrating investment on visitors increases the losses the island suffers during a security crisis.
preview_effects: Development Policy: Office sector tax income +12%

focuses.title: Export Workshops
focuses.requirements: State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native industrial_complex capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Light manufacturing offers a different export base from tourism. Imported machinery and industrial priorities absorb capital that could otherwise support commercial services.
preview_effects: Development Policy: Office sector tax income -3%

focuses.title: Coastal Services
focuses.requirements: Owned and controlled state with native office capacity. State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native offices capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Commercial offices and reliable public services can support the visitor economy. A larger service centre also requires municipal administration and exposes more revenue to interruption.

focuses.title: Industrial Standards
focuses.description: Standards, quality control and vocational instruction help small firms reach external markets. The programme consolidates the manufacturing route instead of duplicating the service investment.

focuses.title: Water for the Island
focuses.requirements: State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native infrastructure capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Water storage and distribution protect agriculture and growing towns from seasonal shortages. The same investment can serve villages, exporters and the tourist economy.

focuses.title: Rural Cooperatives
focuses.description: Cooperatives can pool credit, storage and marketing for small producers. Public supervision and guarantees add fiscal responsibilities while broadening access to investment.

focuses.title: Commercial Credit
focuses.description: Private credit can channel savings toward expanding businesses. A more selective commercial system favours profitable borrowers and leaves some small producers dissatisfied.
preview_effects: Development Policy: Office sector tax income +8%

focuses.title: Land Improvement
focuses.requirements: Owned and controlled state. Communal works agreement accepted. State146 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native infrastructure capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Irrigation and access works can raise rural output without taking communal land through administrative fiat. Projects in sensitive districts require the agreement of the affected representatives.

focuses.title: Small Firm Expansion
focuses.requirements: State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native industrial_complex capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: A second stage of investment can connect small firms to machinery and export finance. Its assets remain national gains even if a later government changes economic policy.

focuses.title: A Commercial Gateway
focuses.requirements: Province 11984 is owned and controlled, coastal and below its native naval-base cap. State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native naval_base capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Improved port facilities can serve exports and essential imports. Reliable handling, storage and coastal access will support the commercial routes on which the island depends.
preview_effects: Development Policy: Office sector tax income +5%

focuses.title: Recovery and Housing
focuses.requirements: Actual displacement has occurred. The state is owned and controlled. State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native infrastructure capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: If conflict disrupts the economy, housing, services and lost commercial links become urgent priorities. Relief must be directed toward the disruption that actually occurred.

focuses.title: Reserves for a Crisis
focuses.requirements: Cyprus has not suffered the conflict damage addressed by Recovery and Housing.
focuses.description: Emergency reserves and redundant supply contracts make peaceful development less vulnerable to pressure. Keeping resources in reserve reduces the return available from ordinary commercial investment.
preview_effects: Development Policy: Office sector tax income -3%

focuses.title: The National Guard
focuses.description: The Guard needs training, communications and a command responsible to the republic. A modest defence programme must distinguish useful readiness from politically dangerous dependence.

focuses.title: Territorial Defence
focuses.description: Local defensive plans can make a small force harder to dislodge from important positions. The resulting posture sacrifices offensive flexibility and cannot promise control of the sea.

focuses.title: Mobile Reserves
focuses.description: A trained mobile reserve can respond to threats before isolated positions are overwhelmed. It requires longer instruction and a continuing readiness budget.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Prepared Positions
focuses.requirements: Both provinces are owned and controlled. Each fort is below its native cap. State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native bunker capacity and cap available. State146 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native coastal_bunker capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Limited fieldworks can protect selected approaches and landing sites. Their value depends on the forces available to hold them and on the geography represented by the current map.

focuses.title: Signals and Logistics
focuses.description: Reliable communications and maintenance improve the usefulness of a reserve force. The programme favours coordination and endurance over additional formations.

focuses.title: Infantry Training
focuses.description: Infantry training and equipment standards must reflect the Guard that Cyprus can actually sustain. Modernization will improve existing forces without conjuring new divisions.

focuses.title: Commando Training
focuses.description: A small specialist arm can cover difficult terrain and demanding missions. Its soldiers require longer training and dedicated support, limiting how widely the model can be applied.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week
Defence Programme: Special forces training time +10%

focuses.title: Civil Defence Network
focuses.description: Shelters, evacuation planning and medical coordination can reduce civilian exposure during a crisis. The network commits resources that cannot also fund a larger specialist force.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Defence Doctrine
focuses.description: The Guard should train around the island, its available forces and its political obligations. A coherent doctrine can reconcile the selected defence posture with realistic national resources.

focuses.title: Coastal Watch
focuses.description: Coastal observation and civilian reporting can improve warning. They provide information to the Guard without pretending that Cyprus can build a great-power fleet.

focuses.title: Non-Aligned Partners
focuses.description: Cyprus and Yugoslavia share the diplomatic traditions of the Non-Aligned Movement. A technical and commercial arrangement can build on that connection without becoming a military alliance.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Base Area Access
focuses.description: Civil access, employment and services around the British Sovereign Base Areas need practical agreements. Accommodation can protect livelihoods while leaving British sovereignty over the bases intact.

focuses.title: Inspected Arms Supply
focuses.description: Czechoslovak supply offers an alternative source of equipment and expertise. UN inspection and agreed storage can reduce the resulting tension at the cost of secrecy and autonomy.
focuses.historicity: Later historical precedent. Earlier negotiated terms are deliberate alternate history.

focuses.title: European Association
focuses.description: Association can open commercial opportunities without granting Community membership. A trade agreement must secure the approval of the actual Community partners and preserve its negotiated conditions.
focuses.historicity: Later historical precedent. Earlier negotiated terms are deliberate alternate history.

focuses.title: Civilian Greek Links
focuses.description: Education and civilian technical cooperation with Greece need not place the Guard under political tutelage. Both governments must fund the exchange and accept its civilian character.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Guarantees with Turkey
focuses.requirements: A communal safeguards agreement has been accepted by both communal delegations.
focuses.description: A confidence agreement with Turkey can reduce external fears once communal guarantees are credible. It supplements Turkish Cypriot consent and cannot replace it.

focuses.title: Presidential Service
focuses.description: The presidential centre can coordinate a broad coalition around independence. A stronger secretariat improves political direction but increases the cost of administration.

focuses.title: A Republican Coalition
focuses.description: The presidential centre can propose a cooperation agreement with EDEK around independence and social provision. The parties must negotiate a common programme and preserve their distinct political organizations.

focuses.title: Church Social Covenant
focuses.description: Parish institutions can help deliver social support and strengthen the presidency in rural society. Public cooperation also reinforces the Church role in education and public life.

focuses.title: A Secular Civil Service
focuses.description: Professional recruitment can improve technical administration beyond confessional or personal networks. The reform weakens some of the political instruments on which a presidential coalition relies.

focuses.title: Parish Relief Network
focuses.description: Reliable parish relief can reach families outside the largest towns. Public funding formalizes the partnership while retaining the educational compromise of the social covenant.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week

focuses.title: Merit Appointments
focuses.description: Technical appointments and open examinations can turn professional administration into a durable advantage. The presidency accepts the limits that impartial recruitment places on patronage.

focuses.title: An Independent State
focuses.description: The presidency can seek support abroad without placing Cyprus under a foreign political command. Independence remains a negotiating position that must be sustained through institutions and resources.

focuses.title: Sovereignty First
focuses.description: A firm central position can resist outside pressure and defend the recognized republic. It makes communal concessions harder to negotiate and reduces confidence in a shared settlement.

focuses.title: A Negotiated Centre
focuses.description: The centre can invest its political authority in a bicommunal agreement. A more complex government may buy confidence and investment at a continuing administrative cost.

focuses.title: Diplomatic Corps
focuses.description: A professional diplomatic service can broaden the republic external options. Representation abroad is a continuing administrative commitment, even when it protects room for manoeuvre.

focuses.title: Settlement Investment
focuses.requirements: The communal settlement is accepted and Cyprus is at peace. State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native industrial_complex capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Investment linked to an accepted settlement can demonstrate that compromise produces tangible national gains. Construction remains conditional on control, capacity and the agreed safeguards.

focuses.title: Constitutional Succession
focuses.description: The presidential centre needs lawful continuity beyond Makarios himself. A durable parliamentary organization and clear constitutional succession can preserve independence through a change of leadership.

focuses.title: Enterprise and Law
focuses.description: Clerides centre-right current can support private enterprise under a republican legal order. Reforms favouring commercial initiative will face criticism over the distribution of their gains.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Office sector tax income +8%

focuses.title: Independent Institutions
focuses.description: Predictable courts and professional administration can protect investment and lawful opposition. The reform depends on initial spending and limits discretionary political favours.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Foreign influence defence +5%

focuses.title: Open Capital Markets
focuses.description: Foreign capital can finance expansion beyond the island limited savings. Greater reliance on outside investors also increases exposure to external political and commercial pressure.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Civilian factory construction +15%
Eniaion Economic Programme: Office sector tax income +8%
Eniaion Economic Programme: Foreign influence defence -10%

focuses.title: National Enterprise
focuses.description: A domestic enterprise strategy can retain local control and improve production standards. Restricted access to outside capital slows the pace at which the building sector can expand.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Military factory output +10%
Eniaion Economic Programme: Production efficiency cap +10%

focuses.title: Commercial Services
focuses.requirements: State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native offices capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Professional services can complement tourism and external commerce. Their expansion increases demand for educated staff and should not be confused with an instant offshore-finance boom.

focuses.title: Domestic Supply Chains
focuses.requirements: State145 owned and controlled by Cyprus; native industrial_complex capacity and cap available.
focuses.description: Local suppliers and common quality standards can strengthen manufacturing. Reliable contracts and technical training will help island firms compete for a greater share of export production.

focuses.title: The Republican Right
focuses.description: A republican right can distinguish constitutional competition from coercive Enosis. Its support for independence leaves room for close cultural relations with Greece.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Political power gain +5%

focuses.title: Settlement Pragmatism
focuses.description: A negotiated settlement can reduce uncertainty for households and businesses. Compromise on communal powers has a political cost among voters seeking firmer national guarantees.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Political power gain -5%

focuses.title: Security Before Terms
focuses.description: Negotiations can be conditioned on stronger security guarantees. The position supports defence and bargaining leverage while requiring more resources and delaying communal confidence.
preview_effects: Expense +0.002% of current Cyprus GDP per week
Eniaion Economic Programme: Foreign influence defence +10%

focuses.title: An Island-Wide Market
focuses.requirements: A mobility agreement is accepted by both communal delegations.
focuses.description: Agreed access can make the island a larger effective market without requiring communities to abandon their institutions. Commercial benefits depend on the mobility settlement remaining credible.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Office sector tax income +8%

focuses.title: Reserve Standards
focuses.description: A capable reserve gives substance to demands for security. Longer training and continuing readiness remain part of the price of this approach.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Unit training time +5%

focuses.title: Constitutional Right
focuses.description: The movement around Clerides can become a lasting constitutional alternative to the presidential centre. Its programme connects private enterprise, a republican legal order and a negotiated national settlement.
preview_effects: Eniaion Economic Programme: Political power gain +5%

focuses.title: Organized Labour
focuses.description: AKEL draws strength from organized workers and a parliamentary commitment to independence. Its social programme improves security for households while placing greater demands on commercial returns.

focuses.title: Parliamentary Strategy
focuses.description: A parliamentary strategy can connect the labour movement to the republic institutions. Opposition rights, coalition bargaining and electoral organization can extend its influence while preserving constitutional competition.
preview_effects: AKEL Social Programme: Political power gain +10%
AKEL Social Programme: Foreign influence defence +5%

focuses.title: A Cooperative Sector
focuses.description: Cooperative credit and marketing can strengthen small producers alongside organized labour. Public oversight and guarantees increase administrative responsibilities.

focuses.title: Public Industry

focuses.description: Public holdings can concentrate scarce investment on industrial capacity. Acquisitions and management must be financed, and political ownership does not remove production constraints.

focuses.title: Rural Processing

focuses.description: Processing and storage can retain more of the value of rural exports on the island. The investment complements cooperative organization and remains useful after a change of government.

focuses.title: Public Standards
focuses.description: Technical standards and professional management can improve public industrial performance. The programme develops the selected public-holdings route while retaining its administrative costs.

focuses.title: Services for All
focuses.description: Wider access to education and health care can support both social confidence and technical skills. The commitment requires continuing public expenditure instead of a one-time declaration.

focuses.title: Bicommunal Labour
focuses.description: Trade-union contacts can rebuild practical cooperation between Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot workers. A common labour agenda asks the party to spend political capital on compromise.
preview_effects: AKEL Social Programme: Political power gain -5%

focuses.title: Eastern Technical Methods
focuses.description: Eastern industrial methods can offer another source of technical knowledge. A stronger reliance on this model narrows diplomatic flexibility without automatically making Cyprus a Soviet ally.

focuses.title: Common Social Rights
focuses.requirements: Both communal delegations accept access and labour safeguards.
focuses.description: Agreed social rights can give cooperation a material foundation across the communal divide. Services must be funded and administered with the consent of both sides.

focuses.title: Planning School
focuses.description: A planning school can train the administrators needed for the public industrial programme. It expands domestic expertise at an additional educational cost.

focuses.title: Democratic Socialism
focuses.description: A durable social programme must win support within the republic political system. Labour rights, public services and national independence can form a common platform for continued democratic competition.

starting_spirits.name: Broken Constitutional Partnership
starting_spirits.remedy: Removed by A Durable Republic after the constitutional settlement operates.
starting_spirits.basis: Joint institutions ceased to operate normally after the 1963 breakdown. This is an institutional condition, not an ethnic characteristic.
starting_spirits.description: The constitutional partnership has broken down. Representation, executive powers and security remain disputed, weakening the authority of common institutions.

starting_spirits.name: Separate Communal Administrations
starting_spirits.remedy: Open Island Routes, after both communal delegations accept
starting_spirits.basis: Separate institutions and restricted access fragment public services and rural markets. These are institutional costs, not ethnic characteristics. The1970 map has no accurate enclave mosaic.
starting_spirits.description: Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot communities rely on separate administrations and restricted routes. Fragmented services and markets raise costs and obstruct shared investment.

starting_spirits.name: Divided National Guard Command
starting_spirits.basis: External officer dependence and competing loyalties undermine unified command.
starting_spirits.description: Dependence on Greek officers and competing political loyalties complicate civilian control of the National Guard. Training and command reforms require time and resources.

starting_spirits.name: Enosis Underground Networks
starting_spirits.remedy: Restore Civilian Rule, after actual network dismantling
starting_spirits.basis: The National Front is relevant at the start. EOKA B is introduced only after its formation in 1971.
starting_spirits.description: Armed supporters of union with Greece challenge the authority of the republic. Clandestine intimidation and violence weaken lawful political competition.

starting_spirits.name: Limited Technical Capacity
starting_spirits.basis: The small technical and educational base constrains specialist capacity. No workforce-size penalty.
starting_spirits.description: Ministries, schools and industry compete for a limited pool of trained specialists. Technical education must expand if national development is to continue.

starting_spirits.name: Makarios Presidential Authority
starting_spirits.remedy: Removed when Makarios leaves the presidency.
starting_spirits.basis: An independent president and archbishop with a broad electoral mandate; not a DIKO government in 1970.
starting_spirits.description: Makarios combines the presidency with the authority of the Orthodox archbishopric. His broad personal mandate can hold together allies with different political aims.

starting_spirits.name: UNFICYP Presence
starting_spirits.remedy: Remains with the actual peacekeeping arrangement
starting_spirits.basis: The peacekeeping force and its de-escalatory role predate 1970.
starting_spirits.description: The United Nations force helps prevent renewed communal fighting and maintains channels between the sides. Its presence encourages restraint during local security disputes.

starting_spirits.name: 1960 Treaty of Guarantee
starting_spirits.remedy: Held by Cyprus, Greece, Turkey and the United Kingdom. Treaty revision requires the participants.
starting_spirits.basis: The same treaty appears for all four parties. No free defence guarantee, automatic war or permanent combat bonus.
starting_spirits.description: The1960 settlement protects the independence and territorial integrity of Cyprus and prohibits union or partition. Greece, Turkey and Britain undertake to consult when the treaty order is threatened.

crisis.title: January 1970
crisis.text: Makarios; Greek junta; communal confidence 35; officer penetration 45. The Treaty appears on all four countries. There is no separate Turkish Cypriot sovereign state.

crisis.title: Two Security Strategies
crisis.text: Cypriot Command reduces officer penetration 15 and temporarily costs organization 5%. Greek mission requires GRE acceptance and grants organization 8% / training time -10%, but penetration +15.

crisis.title: Cypriot Command
crisis.text: Domestic professionalization and police counterweights. Stronger resistance to a coup, slower training and real administrative costs.

crisis.title: Greek Training Mission
crisis.text: The mission never grants Greece a unilateral government change. The Greek player must separately choose political interference.

crisis.title: The Greek Exclusive Paths
crisis.text: Honour the Republic excludes The Officer Network. The network focus costs 50 PP and 0.25% Cyprus GDP, adds 20 penetration and requires an actual junta and officer footprint. Withdraw the Network then excludes Overthrow Makarios.

crisis.title: Overthrow Makarios
crisis.text: The Greek coup focus costs 100 PP and 0.5% Cyprus GDP; penetration must reach 60. A 14-day warning event precedes resolution. Cyprus defences come from its completed focus path. No crisis decision menu or daily meter.

crisis.title: Constitutional Government Survives
crisis.text: Coup strength equals penetration. Defence=40+25 if Presidential Safeguards was completed. Written Mission Terms and Expose Armed Networks reduce penetration before resolution. Defender wins ties. No paid counter-decision or extra response menu.

crisis.title: Coup Government in Nicosia
crisis.text: Only a resolved successful attempt changes the CYP government to the authored Sampson regime. No annexation, no free armies, no automatic war. A restoration choice remains available.

crisis.title: Article IV Consultation
crisis.text: Response events carry 14-day offers. Silence is abstention. Small guarantor focus forks determine mediation or restraint. Coordinated terms need each real signature. Treaty status does not suspend like a paid commercial agreement.

crisis.title: Restoration and Negotiation
crisis.text: Ceasefire/restoration needs the actual belligerents. Communal constitutional terms need separate local acceptance. No automatic province transfer or restoration of one-time assets.

crisis.title: Turkish Intervention or Restraint
crisis.text: Intervene in Cyprus starts the real war and 180 days of naval organization +15%, invasion preparation +50%, amphibious attack +15%, planning speed +30% and maximum planning +20%. Refusal or an unresolved 30-day deadline starts Angry General Staff.

crisis.title: Actual Territorial and Civilian Consequences
crisis.text: Only actual combat/control/displacement enables relief, loss of tourism revenue and later settlement routes. State 146 is a coarse map unit, not the 1970 enclave geography. A separate-state declaration requires a new RP choice and diplomatic consequences, never an automatic 1983 release.

crisis.title: Angry General Staff
crisis.text: 180 days: stability -10%, army organization -10%, political-power gain -15%. Pressure 70. A memorandum at day 30 adds 15; at day 60 a coup succeeds at 60 or more. Two once-only actions remove 25 pressure each, allowing a civilian-control settlement.

crisis.title: Civilian Authority Restored
crisis.text: Reassign commanders and secure a parliamentary mandate, then reassert civilian authority. This closes the coup chain without declaring war and replaces the angry-army penalty with 90 days of command reorganization.

crisis.title: Military Takeover Risk
crisis.text: Unaddressed pressure 60 or more at day 60 brings a native military-junta government. The danger is stated in advance. No daily random roll and no automatic extra war.

crisis.title: Authorize the Cyprus Operation
crisis.text: Intervention during the army confrontation removes the refusal penalty and starts the same guarded Cyprus operation. The 180-day military bonus cannot be renewed through repeated authorizations.

crisis.title: Actual Turkish Intervention
crisis.text: An actual Turkish declaration of war activates the operation. Only this war outcome opens Greece military-support fork; Turkish civilian-control measures or peaceful restraint do not.

crisis.title: The Greek Exclusive Choice
crisis.text: After a real Turkish intervention, Greece chooses Volunteers for Cyprus or Fight Beside Cyprus. The two focuses exclude each other; volunteer aid keeps NATO status, direct war causes both temporary exits.

crisis.title: Volunteers for Cyprus
crisis.text: Volunteer limit +2, minimum army-size requirement -100%, tension requirement -100%. Cyprus must accept the real deployment; no divisions are created. Greece remains outside the war and both countries keep existing NATO membership.

crisis.title: Greek-Turkish War
crisis.text: Snapshot both memberships, remove both through native NATO_leave, then add Greece to the Cyprus side. Neither is a NATO member for this war. Cyprus must be at war with Turkey; no automatic faction annexation or new NATO call.

crisis.title: Peace and NATO Return
crisis.text: When Greece-Turkey AND Cyprus-Turkey hostilities end, both prior members automatically return through NATO_join. Unrelated foreign wars do not define the end. Exceptional incompatible states retain a pending return; monthly fallback does not poll daily.

actor_focuses.title: Officers on Cyprus
actor_focuses.requirements: Greece and Cyprus exist; an actual Greek officer footprint exists.

actor_focuses.title: The Officer Network
actor_focuses.requirements: Greece is ruled by the actual military-junta party. Greek officer footprint remains. Once per campaign.

actor_focuses.title: A Guarantor Settlement
effects: Greece, Turkey and Britain receive Guarantor Consultations

actor_focuses.title: Overthrow Makarios
effects: If successful: Sampson becomes the authored coup-government leader
actor_focuses.requirements: Actual Greek junta remains in power. Officer penetration at least 60. Officer footprint exists. Cyprus remains independent and at peace with Greece. Once per campaign.

actor_focuses.title: Consult the Guarantors
effects: Greece and the United Kingdom receive Guarantor Consultations
Intervention deadline: 30 days after consultations fail
actor_focuses.requirements: A real Cyprus constitutional rupture remains unresolved. Greece, Turkey and Britain are treaty parties.
actor_focuses.description: The guarantors must consider the overthrow of the constitutional government and the security of both communities. Consultation opens a short period for an agreed settlement or a Turkish decision to act.

actor_focuses.title: Negotiated Safeguards
effects: If the security crisis remains unresolved: Angry General Staff (180 days)
actor_focuses.requirements: Cyprus and the relevant guarantors must accept the proposed terms. Local communal consent remains separate. An unresolved crisis at the 30-day deadline still produces Angry General Staff and the military-pressure chain.
actor_focuses.description: Seek an accepted constitutional restoration and credible safeguards for the Turkish Cypriot community. Diplomacy avoids an expedition if it resolves the security crisis before the intervention deadline.

actor_focuses.title: Intervene in Cyprus
effects: Expense +0.005% of Turkish GDP per week while the intervention is active
actor_focuses.requirements: Consultations failed and the actual Cyprus security crisis remains unresolved. Turkey and Cyprus are independent and not already at war. The 30-day deadline and refusal consequences are shown before selection.
actor_focuses.description: Order a military operation in Cyprus. Concentrated naval readiness and prepared landing plans favour rapid intervention, but the expedition creates real financial and diplomatic commitments.

actor_focuses.title: Consultation in London
effects: Greece and Turkey receive Guarantor Consultations

actor_focuses.title: A Joint Mediation
actor_focuses.requirements: Greece and Turkey accept coordinated diplomacy through response events.

actor_focuses.title: Limit the Commitment
actor_focuses.requirements: Britain abstains from a joint enforcement commitment; the treaty record remains.

actor_focuses.title: Refuse Intervention
actor_focuses.description: The government refuses an expedition while the Cyprus crisis remains unresolved. It preserves resources and diplomatic restraint, but senior officers challenge its resolve and civilian authority.
actor_focuses.requirements: The Cyprus security crisis is unresolved. This choice immediately starts the military-pressure chain. A coup is possible after 60 days unless civilian control or intervention resolves the confrontation.
actor_focuses.decision_exception: Finite Turkish army crisis only. No Cyprus decision menu.

actor_focuses.title: The Turkish Landing
actor_focuses.description: Turkish forces have entered the Cyprus war. Greece must decide whether to sustain Cyprus through a volunteer mission or enter the conflict as a belligerent.
actor_focuses.requirements: An actual Turkey-Cyprus war from this crisis is active. Greece and Cyprus are independent. Greece is not already fighting Cyprus.

actor_focuses.title: Volunteers for Cyprus
actor_focuses.description: A volunteer mission can assist Cyprus while Greece avoids direct entry into the war. Cyprus must accept the deployment, and the volunteers must come from formations Greece actually possesses.
actor_focuses.requirements: Turkey is at war with Cyprus. Greece is not at war with either country. Cyprus consents through the real volunteer diplomatic action. Native volunteer and diplomatic-action rules still apply.
effects: Expense +0.002% of Greek GDP per week while the mission remains active
Cyprus Volunteer Mission (while the Cyprus mission remains eligible)

actor_focuses.title: Fight Beside Cyprus
actor_focuses.description: Enter the Cyprus war against Turkey. Greece and Turkey leave NATO for the duration of this conflict, and their previous membership is restored once their war and the Cyprus-Turkey war have both ended.
actor_focuses.requirements: The Turkey-Cyprus war is active. Greece is not already at war with Turkey or Cyprus. Entry must place Greece alongside Cyprus. The temporary NATO exit and return are disclosed to both countries before entry.
effects: Greece and Turkey leave NATO technology sharing and mutual military access
Other NATO members: opinion of Greece -20
Other NATO members: opinion of Turkey -20
Greece joins Cyprus in the war against Turkey
After Greece-Turkey and Cyprus-Turkey peace: Greece returns to NATO
After Greece-Turkey and Cyprus-Turkey peace: Turkey returns to NATO
After related peace, Greece: Daily Pro-Western Support +0.02
After related peace, Greece: Defensive war stability +3%
After related peace, Greece: War support +2%
After related peace, Turkey: Daily Pro-Western Support +0.02
After related peace, Turkey: Defensive war stability +3%
After related peace, Turkey: War support +2%
After related peace: both return to NATO technology sharing and mutual military access

reconciliation: Monthly fixed-tag fallback plus targeted transition hooks. No daily or weekly relationship polling.

geometry.source: Native GUI card bounds verified; grid-to-pixel conversion is a preview approximation. Native font and connector routing remain unverified.

decision_policy: No Cyprus decision menus. Latest user exception: finite Turkey-only army crisis decisions.

intervention.eligibility: Only this campaign crisis, after a real constitutional rupture and failed guarantor consultation. Resolved security terms cancel the countdown and military plot. No pressure merely for an ordinary peaceful disagreement.
intervention.activation: Refuse Intervention starts the army crisis immediately. Inaction or failed negotiations starts it when the 30-day deadline expires. A successful real settlement avoids it.
intervention.pressure_is_not_random: No daily drift or random daily coup roll. Pressure starts at 70, each of two once-only measures removes25, the day30 memorandum adds15, and day60 resolves the disclosed thresholds.
intervention.intervention_commitment: Military bonuses start only with an actual declared Turkish intervention. They end at180days or related peace, whichever occurs first. A reversal from restraint reuses the original crisis receipt and never refreshes a used bonus or setup grant.
intervention.crisis_cancellation: All deadlines are relative to army-crisis activation, not the original consultation date. Explicit refusal activates immediately; no-action or failed diplomacy activates after the30-day intervention window. Any successful intervention, accepted security resolution or completed civilian-control settlement marks the army-crisis instance closed before removing the spirit. All pending30/60/180-day outcomes require the same still-active instance and therefore become no-ops. The original180-day intervention expiry receipt is separate and cannot be restarted.
intervention.coup_outcome: At day60: pressure>=60 installs the dated native military-junta government; pressure36..59 produces a defeated plot and stability-5%; pressure<=35 with the two control measures defeats the plot. A takeover does not automatically declare another war.
intervention.scheduler: One-shot crisis events at30,60and180days. Flags/instance receipts discard stale events. Existing monthly fallback only; no new daily or weekly relationship observer.
intervention.historical_status: The Angry General Staff refusal response and simultaneous full NATO exits/automatic returns are requested RP alternate history. Historical Greece left integrated military command in1974, remained an Alliance member, and returned to the integrated structure in1980.

nato.exit_trigger: Greek direct-war focus, not Turkey initial intervention or the Greek volunteer choice
order: Validate current crisis, participants and war sides
Snapshot actual Greek and Turkish NATO status and current faction
Apply NATO_leave only to actual NATO members
Join Greece to the Cyprus side against Turkey
Create one restoration receipt for each prior member
nato.return_delay_maximum: Next monthly fallback if no peace-resolution hook ran
safeguards: Both countries must still exist and be independent
NATO must have a real living faction leader
Block NATO_join, NATO_join_via_event and stale accession acceptance while this separation receipt remains war-active
Do not join a faction while fighting its members
Do not overwrite a different intervening faction
Do not replay exit/join through repeated events
Retain pending restoration if exceptional engine state blocks return
nato.native_bookkeeping: Use the shared helpers for idea, technology sharing, array, opinion, military access and faction changes. No manual member-array edits.
nato.article_five: Both leave before Greece joins the war, preventing the ordinary member-versus-nonmember NATO war reaction from treating this entry as an attack on a current ally.

crisis_decisions.title: Reassign Exposed Commanders
crisis_decisions.requirements: Angry General Staff crisis active. Not already used. Civilian government remains.

crisis_decisions.title: Secure a Parliamentary Mandate
crisis_decisions.requirements: Angry General Staff crisis active. Not already used. Civilian government remains.

crisis_decisions.title: Reassert Civilian Authority
crisis_decisions.requirements: Both control measures are completed. Military pressure at most 35. The coup has not succeeded.

crisis_decisions.title: Authorize the Cyprus Operation
crisis_decisions.requirements: The same Cyprus security crisis remains unresolved. Turkey has not intervened in this crisis and is not already at war with Cyprus.
effects: Expense +0.005% of Turkish GDP per week while the intervention is active
